news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling closes £2.8m funding gap and secures audit approval as merger plans paused
news_drafts.lead: Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council has eliminated a previously forecast £2.8m medium-term funding gap and won an unqualified audit opinion on its 2025-26 accounts, with auditors identifying no significant weaknesses in its financial arrangements. The council has moved from reliance on reserve depletion to planned contributions to reserves, demonstrating improved financial resilience. However, the council's largest capital project, the £19.4m Angel Centre development, still lacks a finalised financing strategy and full affordability analysis, with members to receive strengthened reporting on borrowing implications. The project's planning permission has been approved, but construction cannot proceed until funding and governance approvals are secured. The council faces heightened governance risks during 2026-27 following the government's 7 September pause to local government reorganisation decisions; it had been scheduled to merge with Maidstone, Sevenoaks and Tonbridge Wells into a West Kent unitary authority from summer 2026. Auditors found no evidence the council had depleted reserves ahead of the planned merger.

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling eliminates £2.8m funding gap as medium-term finances improve
news_drafts.lead: Tonbridge and Malling has eliminated a previously forecast £2.8 million medium-term funding gap and approved a balanced budget for 2026-27, moving from planned reserve depletion to planned reserve contributions, the council's auditors reported to the Audit Committee on 28 September. Grant Thornton expects to issue an unqualified opinion on the 2025-26 financial statements with no significant weaknesses identified in value for money arrangements. The improved position follows a more favourable Local Government Finance Settlement and updated financial assumptions. However, the council's largest planned capital investment—the £19.4 million Angel Centre project, with £15.0 million profiled for 2026-27—has incomplete financing strategy, and borrowing may be required. The government's pause on local government reorganisation decisions announced on 7 September, which affects the council's planned merger into a West Kent unitary authority, creates heightened risks for financial stewardship and governance during 2026-27 and 2027-28.

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling eliminates £2.8m funding gap and expects unqualified audit, as Angel Centre financing strategy remains incomplete.
news_drafts.lead: Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council has closed a previously forecast £2.8m shortfall in its medium-term finances and approved a balanced budget for 2026-27, moving from reliance on reserve depletion to planned contributions to reserves. External auditors intend to issue an unqualified opinion on the 2025-26 financial statements with no significant weaknesses in value for money. However, the council's largest planned capital investment, the Angel Centre at £19.4m total cost, remains without a finalised financing strategy. Auditors raised an improvement recommendation to strengthen councillor reporting on the project's borrowing requirements and affordability implications. The council is merging with three neighbours into a West Kent unitary authority from summer 2026, a decision announced in July but paused for review by government on 7 September. Auditors found the council ran down no reserves ahead of the merger and identified no evidence of that known risk.

findings.paper_title: Annex 1 - Supplementary report - Pensions asset ceiling
findings.headline: The pension liability position is subject to material unquantifiable swings that could significantly change year-on-year.
findings.detail: The asset ceiling adjustment depends on future contribution rates and contribution arrangements. The council states that changes following the 2026-29 contribution certificate could result in material movement even if the underlying Pension Fund remains strongly funded. The council explicitly acknowledges it cannot quantify the effect of changing contribution rates and that it is reasonably possible outcomes in the next financial year will require material adjustment to the reported pension position.
findings.matters: Lenders and other councils need to understand that the pension liability in the accounts carries significant uncertainty; the figure could swing substantially and is not a reliable forecast of year-end position.
findings.figures: Effect unquantified; material movement possible; material adjustment reasonably possible in next year
findings.quote: It is not possible to quantify the effect of a change in future contribution rates on the asset ceiling, as this would require additional actuarial information that was not available at the date the accounts were authorised for issue. It is reasonably possible that outcomes within the next financial year will require a material adjustment to the net defined benefit position.

findings.paper_title: Annex 1 - Supplementary report - Pensions asset ceiling
findings.headline: The council's pension fund has a £16.3m surplus that cannot be recognized as an asset due to IFRIC14, resulting in a reported £2.4m liability instead.
findings.detail: As at 31 March 2026, the council's pension fund showed an unadjusted surplus of £16.292m. However, IFRIC14 accounting rules restrict recognition of this benefit to the present value of economic benefit available through future contribution reductions. On this basis, no economic benefit is assessed as available, and a £17.462m asset ceiling adjustment results in the fund position being recorded as a net liability of £2.430m instead of a surplus.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders reviewing the council's balance sheet need to understand that the reported pension liability materially understates the fund's actual position, and that this gap creates volatility in reported financial position.
findings.figures: Unadjusted funding surplus £16.292m; asset ceiling adjustment £17.462m; net pension liability £2.430m
findings.quote: In accordance with IFRIC14, the amount recognised is restricted to the present value of the economic benefit available through reductions in future contributions...On that basis no economic benefit is assessed as available and an asset ceiling adjustment of £17.462m has been made, resulting in a net pension liability of £2.430m.

findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation deferral announced early September 2026; unitary council to begin March 2028, reducing immediate uncertainty but structural change confirmed
findings.detail: LGR will end Tonbridge and Malling in March 2028. Recent deferral announcement in early September 2026 has reduced immediate uncertainty. Risk of operational shortfall from staff departures persists. New unitary council may be burdened with historic county debt. Shared strategic partner being procured to support collaboration through Vesting Day April 2028. Close working at Leader and Chief Executive level. Risk score 16.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether the council has leadership stability through 2028, whether debt obligations are being managed, and what structural changes will affect successor council creditworthiness
findings.figures: Vesting Day April 2028; LGR deferral announced early September 2026; risk score 16
findings.quote: Recent announcement on deferal of LGR in early September 2026 has resulted in longer term risk being reduced

findings.headline: Managed exit from Agile system and transition back to Uniform — new operational risk with data transfer and staffing implications
findings.detail: Council executing managed exit from Agile system with return to Uniform system. PID signed with IDOX establishing technical requirements for data return. Clear project plan with achievable milestones. Post-implementation review being carried out by internal audit with live lessons learned being implemented. Continued monitoring by implementation staff. Risk identified September 2026. Risk score 12.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether the council's planning and regulatory systems remain stable during this transition and whether there are risks to data integrity
findings.figures: Risk identified September 2026; risk score 12; PID signed with IDOX
findings.quote: Failure to deliver a managed exit from Agile and transition back to Uniform System

findings.headline: Staff recruitment and retention pressures addressed with 4% pay award agreed February 2026
findings.detail: Loss of capacity due to staff retirements (workforce age profile), staff departures to higher-paying roles, recruitment difficulties in key professional roles, and uncertainty from Local Government Reorganisation. Competition from private sector and London Boroughs. Council agreed 4% pay award in February 2026. Workforce Strategy reviewed June 2026. Market Supplement Policy in use for difficult-to-resource roles. Risk score 16 unmitigated, 12 mitigated.
findings.matters: A lender needs to assess whether the council can maintain service delivery and financial control with stable staffing, and whether pay inflation is sustainable
findings.figures: 4% pay award February 2026; Workforce Strategy reviewed June 2026; risk score 16 unmitigated, 12 mitigated
findings.quote: Pay award of 4% agreed by Council in February 2026 has helped in ensuring that pay remains competitive with others in the County and therefore score has been reduced.
